verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks: A gives a usable, internally reconciled number set: "Net debt (30 Jun 2026) $26,912m", "Market capitalisation $247,596m ... $159.64 × 1,550.97m", plus a net-debt bridge that reconciles ($24,570m − $1,196m = $23,374m; + $3,538m = $26,912m). It also covers H1 2026 and Q2 2026 (+5% CER), the CARDIO-TTRansform failure of 9 July 2026, the NYSE listing harmonisation, and answers the three brief questions (US pricing, patent cliff, oncology) with explicit workings and named gaps.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks: B has machine-traceable XBRL citations for every income-statement and balance-sheet line, a geographic revenue split ("United States 24.0 / China 6.64 / Japan 3.56"), and an unusually frank self-audit: it publishes its own failed validators ("cited figure agreement ... fail", "source coverage 0.8824") and eight red-team challenges, including that year-one FCF of ~$20.5bn is ~1.74x FY2025 actual FCF.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_: A, because a reader can trust and reuse its numbers without the interface: price, share count, net debt, market cap and multiples all cross-check, and it states its gaps precisely. B's headline is self-defeating — it prints two base cases $357.62 and $158.58, a 5.6% WACC built on book equity weights it admits makes "every valuation discounted at it correspondingly too high", and a garbage segment cell ("Other Europe | ,Ó") — so nothing in its valuation can be taken at face value.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks: A ties nearly every figure to a named filing with a URL and shows the arithmetic: e.g. "FCF yield (OCF less capex, FY2025) 4.57% | ($14,575m − $3,270m) ÷ $247,596m", and a Validation section that reconciles the net debt bridge ($24,570m − $1,196m = $23,374m; + $3,538m = $26,912m) and explicitly discards bad third-party data ("Dukascopy's enterprise value is wrong ... I discard its market-cap, EV and P/E figures"). It also covers H1 2026, Q2 2026 CER +5%, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure, and the NYSE ordinary-share listing change — none of which appear in B.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks: B exposes its own machine-checkable audit trail — every number cites a formula and a stored calculation (e.g. "Calculated: `WACC = Ke * E/(D+E) + Kd_after_tax * D/(D+E)` = 0.0562"), plus a red-team log that flags the model's own incoherence: "projected revenue of ~USD 103.2bn ... yet projected EBIT of ~USD 14.7bn ... implying operating margin collapses from ~23.4% to roughly half". It also carries a geographic revenue split from the 20-F that A admits it could not source ("I could not extract the equivalent FY2025 non-US regional split").
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_: A, without hesitation. Every material figure in A can be walked back to a specific 6-K, 20-F or RNS, the cross-checks are shown, and gaps are named rather than filled with guesses. B's own validators report failures ("cited figure agreement ... fail", "source coverage ... fail"), its base case spans $158 to $358, and its headline DCF rests on a book-value equity weight and a beta of 0.27 that its own red team calls indefensible — a sceptic cannot get from that output to anything checkable.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks: A gives an actionable, priced view with a decomposed disagreement: "Probability-weighting bear ($71), base ($127) and bull ($203) at 25/50/25 gives $132, a −17.3% capital return", plus a reverse-DCF stating exactly what the market pays for ("a cost of equity of 7.20% ... or a 3.90% perpetual growth rate ... or a sustained operating cash-flow margin of 30.8%"). It also carries current-period facts B lacks entirely — H1 2026 revenue $30,672m, Q2 CER +5%, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure and ~9-10% share fall, Farxiga US LOE, and a segment-level answer ("Oncology contributed approximately +6.9 percentage points of group CER growth").
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks: B has a machine-traceable FY2025 geographic revenue split from the 20-F ("United States 24.0 ... China 6.64 ... Japan 3.56" USDbn) that A explicitly could not source, and a longer FY2021–25 margin series. It also publishes an adversarial audit against itself, e.g. "projected revenue of ~USD 103.2bn is nearly double FY2025 revenue, yet projected EBIT of ~USD 14.7bn is barely above FY2025 operating income" — honest, but it is an indictment of its own model.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_: A, without hesitation. B's own validators fail ("cited figure agreement ... fail", "source coverage ... fail"), its two terminal methods produce $357.62 versus $158.58, its beta of 0.27 and book-value equity weight give a 5.6% WACC the document itself calls too low, and it admits its 9.05% growth rate rests on one quarter of management commentary. A, by contrast, states its weakest link plainly ("Cost of equity: 8.5% — an assumption, not a derivation") and still delivers a defensible, sensitised position an investor can act on.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks: A's numbers are almost all traced to primary SEC sources with artefact hashes and verified passages (e.g. the 8-K segment table quoted in full at note [24]), and it publishes an explicit adversarial audit — 'the run's own recorded implied upside is negative 10.4%... none of the listed claims discloses the market capitalisation' — which is a level of self-policing B lacks. It also carries a machine-checked validation table (citation accuracy 1, primary source ratio 0.9418).
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks: B gives the operator an actionable, defensible view: 'Target price $405 ... total expected return of −17.1%', with a 30-cell WACC × g grid where 'Only one of thirty cells ... exceeds the current price', and reverse-DCF framings ('the market's implied WACC is 7.94%, or its implied perpetual growth rate is 5.78%'). It also answers the cloud-margin question with arithmetic A declines to attempt — 'Intelligent Cloud gross margin fell 420bp in FY26 (62.2% → 58.0%)' and the +116bp operating-margin bridge being '100% opex leverage' — plus FY27 guidance, the $329.1bn uncommenced lease stack and the useful-life/capex reclassification.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_: B, first and clearly. It reaches a position, shows the price the market is paying ('the current price is my bull case'), and stress-tests it; A explicitly refuses to state a view, prints two terminal values that 'do not bracket a range; they disagree' by 2.9x, and flags its own unresolved self-contradiction — useful as a caution list but not something I could size a position from. I'd hand A alongside only for its primary-source trail on the FY26 statements.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks: A anchors nearly every figure in primary SEC sources with the exact formula behind it — e.g. note [16] 'Calculated: free cash flow = operating cash flow - capital expenditure = 66987000000 USD for FY2026', and a Cost of Capital table showing beta 1.067513930704 and the derivation 'Kd = interest expense / average debt'. It also publishes a full adversarial critique of itself, including the damning line 'the run's own recorded implied upside is negative 10.4%'.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks: B gives the reader a checkable arithmetic chain and an explicit reconciliation table: 'Segment revenues sum to group total: 139,996 + 137,791 + 54,052 = 331,839 ✓' and 'FY26 capex: 9M $80.146bn + Q4 $35.802bn = $115.948bn, vs FY25 $64.6bn + disclosed $51.4bn increase = $116.0bn ✓'. It also labels its weak numbers rather than burying them — 'The 30 June 2026 balance sheet figures below are therefore drawn from secondary aggregators… and should be verified against the 10-K before use' — and names its assumptions as assumptions ('Equity risk premium 5.0% — This is my assumption, not a sourced figure').
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_: B, first and without hesitation. A cannot be trusted on its own numbers: it states in Historical Financial Analysis that 'no cash flow line — neither operating cash flow nor capital expenditure — is present, so free cash flow cannot be stated at all' while printing $182.9bn OCF and $115.9bn capex elsewhere, describes two reportable segments in one section and three in another, and offers two base-case values ($227.90 and $442.26) with no resolution. B carries one number you can act on ($405 target, −17.1% total return), shows its working, and tells you exactly which cells are weakly sourced.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks: A's figures are individually traceable: each note gives a formula, a rounded value, a publisher, a URL and a retrieval date (e.g. note [24] carries a verified quoted passage from the 8-K segment exhibit with artefact hash `61b3404537d6`), and it publishes an adversarial audit against itself — including that 'the recorded terminal value share is 0.888' and that 'the run's own recorded implied upside is negative 10.4%... none of the listed claims discloses the market capitalisation'. It also discloses a failed validation check and an internal contradiction, both with both sides published.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks: B actually answers the posed questions with arithmetic rather than declaring them unanswerable: 'Intelligent Cloud gross margin fell 420bp in FY26 (62.2% → 58.0%)', a decomposition showing '+116bp' of group margin is '−88bp' gross offset by '+204bp' opex, and a capitalisation magnitude check ('$115.95bn of cash... charged somewhere between $24bn and $44bn'). Where A says of AI revenue only that disclosures 'do not answer' it, B derives '$45.6bn (91%) came from Microsoft Cloud and approximately $29bn (58%) from Azure' and explicitly refuses to estimate beyond that. It also carries dated forward items A omits entirely (A: 'no catalyst can be dated here').
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_: B, first — it takes a position, shows the working behind every derived figure ('calculated here'), and is candid about exactly which cells are unsourced ('§17.2 as unbuilt', balance sheet 'the weakest-sourced part of the note'). A is better wired for citation-chasing and its self-audit is valuable, but it repeatedly concedes it cannot address the questions asked and contradicts itself on whether capex/FCF exist; I would hand A over second as a source-check companion.
